Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.20% today and 1.49% over two weeks, as refiners face margin pressure from weak crude oil pricing and demand signals. US oil dropped to $89.53 per barrel while refineries are running at high capacity (95.7%), a combination that squeezes the profit refiners make on each barrel processed—the spread between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for typically narrows when oil is cheap and supply is plentiful. Even the strong refinery utilization rate can't offset this headwind when input costs fall faster than output prices.

The broader energy landscape offers mixed signals for refiners. Diesel prices remain elevated in some regions (driving UK inflation higher), and geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz are creating long-term supply-chain uncertainty, but neither is translating into an immediate demand boost strong enough to lift margins. The recent permitting reform passage could eventually help energy infrastructure projects, but that's a future benefit—today's price action reflects the immediate squeeze refiners are experiencing.
